attributes.body_ja:
「なり」は、日本語（にほんご）の古風（こふう）な接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）です。「なり」にはいくつかの意味（いみ）がありますが、そのうちの一つは「(A) するとすぐに (B)」や「(A) の瞬間（しゅんかん）に、(B)」というものです。この文型（ぶんけい）は、動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。

(B) に入（はい）る内容（ないよう）は、通常（つうじょう）、強（つよ）い意思（いし）や感情（かんじょう）によって引（ひ）き起（お）こされる、思（おも）いがけない行動（こうどう）です。ほとんどの場合（ばあい）、「なり」は自分自身（じぶんじしん）ではなく他人（たにん）について話（はな）すときに使（つか）われます

豆知識（まめちしき）

「なり」は一見（いっけん）、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「なる」の活用形（かつようけい）のように見（み）えるかもしれません。しかし、実（じつ）はこの「なり」は「形（なり）」という漢字（かんじ）の読（よ）み方（かた）から来（き）ており、「ところ」と同（おな）じように (A) の状況（じょうきょう）全体（ぜんたい）を表（あらわ）します。
attributes.body:
なり is an old-fashioned particle in Japanese that has several different uses. One of those uses is to convey the meaning of 'as soon as (A), (B)', or 'the moment of (A), (B)'. This structure will follow the dictionary form of verbs and is classified as a conjunction particle.

(B) is usually something that is surprising, and brought about by a strong sense of will or emotion. Additionally, なり is almost always used in relation to other people, rather than oneself.

Fun Fact

Despite appearing to be a conjugation of the う-Verb なる 'to become' at first glance, なり is actually one of the readings of 形（なり）, meaning 'shape', and refers to the overall situation of (A) in a similar way to ところ.

attributes.source: A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns

attributes.body: Both describe actions happening immediately after another. かと思ったら・かと思うと adds surprise or contrast, as in 雨が降ったかと思うと止んだ (No sooner had it started raining than it stopped). なり emphasizes immediacy without surprise, as in ドアを開けるなり走り出した (He opened the door and immediately ran out).

attributes.body: Both と同時に and なり follow the plain form of verbs and describe events occurring in close succession, but their nuance differs. と同時に means 'at the same time as' and emphasizes actual simultaneity. In contrast, なり highlights immediate consequence, something happening as soon as the first action occurs, and often implies a reflexive or automatic response.

attributes.body: Both express immediacy following another action, but differ in nuance and tone. たとたんに stresses suddenness or unexpectedness, sometimes with emotion, e.g. '立ち上がったとたんに倒れた' ('He collapsed the moment he stood up'). なり also marks instantaneousness, but feels more formal or literary, and implies a natural cause-effect link, e.g. '席に着くなり、食べ始めた' ('As soon as he sat down, he started eating').

second_relatable.title: なり
second_relatable.meaning: As soon as, The moment, When

attributes.body: Both なり and 次第 indicate immediacy but differ in tone and nuance. なり is a neutral expression suggesting a spontaneous or automatic reaction. For example, 布団に入るなり寝た ('He fell asleep as soon as he got in his futon'). 次第 has a more formal tone and is often used in business contexts to show that something happens immediately after a condition is met. For example, 終わり次第ご連絡します ('I'll contact you as soon as I'm finished').
